use_en: Leaves mashed with olive oil and wine as a plaster; the oil and ointments made from it; the dried plant sprinkled on a whitlow; a cerate made from it.
machine_translation_en: It soothes hot swellings, erysipelas, namla, pustules and ulcers, including those on the palms, and fire burns, with olive oil; so does its wine, and its leaves applied as a plaster after being mashed with oil and wine; so do its oil and the ointments made from its oil. The dried plant helps when sprinkled on a whitlow, and so does the cerate made from it.

use_en: Fruit cooked in wine as a plaster; its ash in a cerate.
machine_translation_en: If its fruit is cooked in wine and made into a plaster, it heals ulcers of the palms and soles and fire burns, and keeps the burn from blistering; so does its ash in a cerate.

use_en: Its water dripped into the ear.
machine_translation_en: It stops nosebleeds, clears scurf, dries ulcers of the head and of the ear and their pus when its water is dripped in, and its wine helps slack gums.
reader_note: Rule found no preparation: 'dripped in' (yuqattar) is not a rule cue.

use_en: With egg white on fire burns.
machine_translation_en: It helps with everything said of myrtle, helps with a whitlow, and with egg white it is put on fire burns and hot swellings.
reader_note: Rule found the vehicle but no preparation form.

use_en: Applied to fresh wounds; its solution and that of its dried root.
machine_translation_en: It eats away dead flesh, closes fresh wounds and sets sprains; its solution and that of its dried root are used for this.

use_en: An ingredient of ointments that fill ulcers.
machine_translation_en: It goes into ointments and fills ulcers and grows flesh in them, and it eats away bad flesh, especially isranj (red lead); isranj is also stronger at growing flesh.
reader_note: Rule missed 'grows flesh in them' (the cue word order differs). Lead compound: historical record only.

use_en: Ash on scaling skin and foul wounds; bark cooked in vinegar for fire burns.
machine_translation_en: Its ash is put on scaling skin and on foul wounds, and they heal; its bark cooked in vinegar helps fire burns.
reader_note: Rule missed 'foul wounds' (al-jirahat al-wasikha) as an infection term.

use_en: Applied to close ulcers and fresh wounds.
machine_translation_en: It agglutinates (closes) ulcers and fresh wounds.
reader_note: 'Agglutinates' (yulziqu) is not a rule cue.

use_en: Leaves as a plaster; pounded and sprinkled on ulcers.
machine_translation_en: A plaster of its leaves helps fire burns and closes large wounds and bad ulcers; pounded and sprinkled on flabby and putrefying ulcers it helps.

use_en: Not stated in this clause.
machine_translation_en: It helps ulcers, especially chafing ulcers between the thighs.
reader_note: No preparation stated; chafing (sahj) ulcers.

use_en: With powdered frankincense, in deep ulcers.
machine_translation_en: It removes tetters and grows flesh in deep ulcers, especially with powdered frankincense. [Next section, joints:] it helps swellings of the muscles.
reader_note: Span runs into the next section: the label 'joints' had no sentence boundary before it.

use_en: With a cerate to close; with terebinth resin and natron for ulcerated scabies.
machine_translation_en: It stops creeping ulcers, closes them with a cerate and cleans foul ulcers; with Nabataean gum and natron it is a remedy for ulcerated scabies, baras and bahaq (white and dark skin patches).
reader_note: Copper salt, caustic: historical record only.

use_en: Decoction poured over fire burns; said to act on wounds like dragon's blood.
machine_translation_en: Its decoction is useful for fire burns when poured over them, and it is said to act on wounds as dragon's blood does; it is put on broken bones alone and with a cerate.
reader_note: The wound use is reported ('it is said'), not asserted by the author.

use_en: Oil with myrtle on the marks left by ulcers.
machine_translation_en: Its oil with myrtle is good for the hair and for the marks of ulcers, and its mucilage helps cold fissures, especially with rose oil; it goes into remedies for freckles, complexion, bad breath and body odour.
reader_note: About scars left by ulcers (cosmetic), not open ulcers.

use_en: Leaves 'given to drink' (yusqa) for carbuncle and fire burns; juice with white lead on erysipelas.
machine_translation_en: It soothes swellings; its leaves are given to drink for carbuncle, fire burns and phlegmatic swellings; its juice with white lead is put on namla and erysipelas, and it is gargled for swollen tonsils.
reader_note: 'Given to drink' for burns is odd: possibly a copying error (OpenITI flags many typos). Check against an edition.

use_en: With honey on a whitlow; husks for ulcer scars; with vinegar and oil as an embrocation.
machine_translation_en: With honey it is put on a whitlow and it goes away; its husks are good for the marks of ulcers; with vinegar and oil as an embrocation it helps the pain called murakkab, a pain in the body like warts with a feeling like creeping ants.
reader_note: The 'ulcer' theme here is about scars (out of scope); the whitlow use is in scope.

use_en: Applied to fresh wounds; with duck or pig fat on tetters; on burn ulcers.
machine_translation_en: It strongly closes wounds, especially fresh wounds, and stops malignant ulcers from spreading; it is put on tetters with duck fat and pig fat, on harfiyya ulcers and on cold fissures, and it mends ulcers that come from burns.
reader_note: Rule missed 'malignant (ulcers) spreading' and the fat vehicles. 'harfiyya' is probably a misspelling of harqiyya (burn ulcers).

use_en: Not stated in this clause.
machine_translation_en: Good for hot swellings, fire burns, namla, urticaria, erysipelas, swellings at the root of the ear and scrofula.
reader_note: No preparation stated.

use_en: Not stated; with Cimolian earth and white lead on erysipelas.
machine_translation_en: Good for malignant ulcers, 'Persian fire', chronic ulcers and deep wounds, and it ranks first among the remedies in these chapters; with Cimolian earth and white lead it helps when put on erysipelas.

use_en: Unreadable.
machine_translation_en: [Garbled: a section label without its colon, then a fragment about fresh leaves of 'jabal al-miskin'.]
reader_note: Corrupt passage (OpenITI MISSING_PARTS); the label words were counted as a theme.

use_en: Cooked in wine for large abscesses; as a plaster with a cerate on fire burns.
machine_translation_en: Cooked in wine it closes large abscesses, and as a plaster it helps fire burns, especially with a cerate, for which it has no equal.
reader_note: Rule missed 'abscesses' (khurajat).

use_en: The base of ointments.
machine_translation_en: It grows flesh in ulcers only incidentally; Galen said it neither cleans nor fouls, neither grows nor reduces flesh, but is the base material of ointments; it helps chafing of the groin and thighs.
reader_note: The text records a disagreement (Galen). Lead oxide: historical record only.

use_en: General property.
machine_translation_en: Cleansing, resolving, astringent and drying ... the burnt kind dries and resolves more, and it prevents putrefaction and helps thick humours.
reader_note: A general property ('prevents putrefaction'), not a wound use.

use_en: With olive oil on fire burns to prevent blistering.
machine_translation_en: It is rubbed on with oil and vinegar near a fire to make one sweat, which calms itching, especially phlegmatic itching; with oil on fire burns it prevents blistering, especially the borax-like and the African kind ...
reader_note: Span is long; the burn clause is the middle part.

use_en: Root kneaded with honey and bitter-vetch flour; powdered with honey on fire burns.
machine_translation_en: Its root kneaded with honey and bitter-vetch flour opens abscesses slow to ripen and is put on wounds and ulcers as a plaster. [Wounds and ulcers:] it dries wounds and joins them strongly, even a cut tendon; powdered with honey it is put on fire burns, wounds of the sinews and deep ulcers; mixed with bitter vetch and honey it cleans the dirt of ulcers.
reader_note: Section label 'wounds and ulcers' inside the span was not split (no sentence boundary before it).

use_en: Root, and leaves cooked, for scalds; best used with rose oil.
machine_translation_en: It fills ulcers with good flesh; its root helps scalds from hot water because it dries and cleans moderately, and so do its leaves cooked; it closes wounds; it is best used with rose oil.

use_en: Not stated (the garden kind).
machine_translation_en: The garden kind is the best of remedies for scalds from hot water.

use_en: Leaves cooked for fire burns; with honey as a liniment; as a plaster on malignant ulcers.
machine_translation_en: Its leaves, cooked, are good for fire burns; as a liniment with honey it helps tetters, and applied as a plaster on malignant ulcers it heals all of that.

use_en: As a plaster.
machine_translation_en: As a plaster it helps foul and malignant ulcers, wounds, ulcerated boils and fire burns.

use_en: Cooked with vinegar; with sea water for spreading ulcers.
machine_translation_en: Cooked with vinegar it fills deep ulcers and removes their foulness so that their dirt lessens, and for large ones with something more astringent such as pomegranate rind; with sea water it is used for spreading ulcers, erysipelas, namla and fissures from cold.

use_en: General property.
machine_translation_en: Bee honey is hot and dry in the second degree ... its power cleanses, opens the mouths of vessels, resolves moisture, draws moisture from deep in the body, and prevents putrefaction in it and the spoiling of meat.
reader_note: General property and food preservation, not a wound use.

use_en: Applied to foul ulcers; boiled until thick to close fresh wounds; with dill on tetters.
machine_translation_en: It cleans foul, hollow ulcers; boiled until thick it joins fresh wounds; smeared on with dill it heals tetters.

use_en: Bark as a plaster or powder; leaves as a powder on wounds.
machine_translation_en: Its bark helps harfiyya ulcers and has a closing power; its bark is astringent enough to heal chafing when put on as a plaster; the powdered bark helps scalds from hot water; its leaves, as a powder, join wounds; its bark suits bruises and closes wounds.
reader_note: 'harfiyya' as in frankincense (probably burn ulcers).

use_en: With honey on bruise marks; closes an ulcerated whitlow.
machine_translation_en: With honey it is put on the marks of blows; it closes an ulcerated whitlow; with wine on falling hair it stops the fall.

body_site: skin and mucosa (anus, genitals, nose, mouth)
use_en: Not stated.
machine_translation_en: Suitable for ulcers that are slow to close, especially at the anus, the genitals, the nose and the mouth, and for fistulas.

use_en: Seeds with honey as a liniment.
machine_translation_en: Pomegranate seeds with honey as a liniment for a whitlow.

use_en: Seeds with honey as a liniment on malignant ulcers; calyces, burnt, for wounds; the flower joins wounds.
machine_translation_en: Pomegranate seeds with honey as a liniment for malignant, rough ulcers; its calyces for wounds, especially burnt; and the flower (jullanar) joins wounds ... [the rest of the clause is about food].
reader_note: Span runs into dietary text.

use_en: Washed (purified) tutty.
machine_translation_en: Its washed form helps ulcers, even cancerous ulcers.
reader_note: 'yafa' is a typo for 'yanfa' (helps). The 'cancerous ulcers' claim is out of scope and not used.

use_en: Wild leaves with olive (oil) for fire burns; decoction poured over.
machine_translation_en: It helps namla and erysipelas; the leaves of the wild kind with olive help fire burns, and so does its decoction poured over; the garden kind helps at the start of a hot swelling ...
reader_note: 'tatwilan' is a typo for 'natulan' (poured over), so the rule missed the form.

use_en: Taken and poured over; as a liniment to prevent swelling.
machine_translation_en: It prevents swellings from forming and gangrene from spreading, heals erysipelas eaten and poured over, stops the spread of every swelling, helps a whitlow, and prevents namla and carbuncle, when painted on before the swelling forms.

use_en: Wool soaked in vinegar on wounds; applied to creeping ulcers and fire burns.
machine_translation_en: Wool soaked in vinegar and put on wounds keeps them from swelling; it helps creeping ulcers from spreading, and scabies and tetter; and it helps fire burns faster than anything.

use_en: Warmed vinegar with salt as an enema.
machine_translation_en: It cools the womb, and warmed vinegar with salt is given as an enema for creeping ulcers of the intestines after soft enemas.
reader_note: Internal (intestinal) ulcers are out of the séance scope (skin wounds, burns, ulcers and skin infection).

use_en: Not stated.
machine_translation_en: It helps fire burns.
